newsitem.title: UK: EMU could fuel UK Liberal-Labour tension.
newsitem.headline: EMU could fuel UK Liberal-Labour tension.

text.p: The European single currency could become a major source of tension between Britain's opposition Labour Party and minority Liberal Democrats, the Liberal's treasury spokesman said on Monday.

Malcolm Bruce told journalists at the Liberal Democrats annual conference in Brighton that the markets appeared to be assuming that a Labour government under Tony Blair would not take Britain into Economic and Monetary Union.
"If Labour's view is that we should not join, we are bound to have a pretty fundamental disagreement," Bruce said.

The conference has so far been dominated by discussions about possible cooperation between Labour and the Liberals after the next election, with party leader Paddy Ashdown saying he would not totally rule out a coalition between the two.

Bruce said he had no personal knowledge of whether Labour would join a single currency, but added: "Looking at the Labour Party's reluctance to make difficult decisions, I think they may want to stay out."

Earlier, Bruce told a news conference: "If the criteria have been met by the core group and by the UK, we are totally committed to the view that the UK must be founder members (of the single currency) and that there is nothing to be gained in staying out in those circumstances."
However, he said the position might be different if the criteria had to be "fudged" in order that certain countries could take part.
